title: Smart Data Models - TM Forum Open APIs - ResourceCandidate
description: ResourceCandidate is an entity that makes a resource specification available to a catalog. A ResourceCandidate and its associated resource specification may be published - made visible - in any number of resource catalogs, or in none. (TM Forum TMF634 Resource Catalog Management 5.0.0, OpenAPI component ResourceCandidate; attribute names kept verbatim except the NGSI-LD reserved terms / JSON-LD keywords renamed with a tmf prefix (id, @type, @baseType, @schemaLocation, ...); deprecated attributes left out.)

type.description: Property. NGSI-LD Entity type. It must be equal to 'ResourceCandidate'

category.description: Relationship. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF634_ResourceCatalog/blob/v5.0.0/TMF634-Resource_Catalog_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/ResourceCandidate/properties/category'. The categories in which this candidate is exposed. In TMF this is an array of ResourceCategoryRef objects; here the NGSI-LD ids of the referenced ResourceCategory entities (urn:ngsi-ld:ResourceCategory:<tmf id>). Inline values and reference metadata (href, name, @referredType) are not kept.

resourceSpecification.description: Relationship. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF634_ResourceCatalog/blob/v5.0.0/TMF634-Resource_Catalog_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/ResourceCandidate/properties/resourceSpecification'. Resources are physical or non-physical components (or some combination of these) within an enterprise's infrastructure or inventory. They are typically consumed or used by services (for example a physical port assigned to a service) or contribute to the realization of a Product (for example, a SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application, Computing and Network domains, and include, for example, Network Elements, software, IT systems, content and information, and technology components. A ResourceSpecification is an abstract base class for representing a generic means for implementing a particular type of Resource. In essence, a ResourceSpecification defines the common attributes and relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource defines a specific instance that is based on a particular ResourceSpecification. In TMF this is a ResourceSpecificationRef object; here the NGSI-LD id of the referenced ResourceSpecification entity (urn:ngsi-ld:ResourceSpecification:<tmf id>). Inline values and reference metadata (href, name, @referredType) are not kept.

externalIdentifier.description: Property. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF634_ResourceCatalog/blob/v5.0.0/TMF634-Resource_Catalog_Management-v5.0.0.oas.yaml#/components/schemas/ResourceCandidate/properties/externalIdentifier'. An identification of an entity that is owned by or originates in a software system different from the current system, for example a ProductOrder handed off from a commerce platform into an order handling system. The structure identifies the system itself, the nature of the entity within the system (e.g. class name) and the unique ID of the entity within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single entity, e.g. if the entity passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system. In this case the consumer is expected to sequence the IDs in the array in reverse order of provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list.
